role: independent Yggdrasil research contributor; not Amalgam native owner
question: Can a learned causal input-output mechanism from environment A accelerate held-action prediction in environment B with unseen parent-variable relocation, while surviving B learning and a byte-exact restore?

worlds.source_A: True causal function on three distinct hidden input bits, unknown operator and parents, with 5% independent deterministic-hash sensor flips. A receives three shuffled rounds of all 32 actions (96 outcomes).
worlds.source_B_shared: Same latent 3-bit truth table and output orientation as A, but source input parents randomly remapped to a DIFFERENT unordered triple of 5 bits. The order of the three causal inputs may also permute. New nuisance/action semantics and new output-noise domain. Learner sees only control vectors and consequence labels, no correspondence map or operator name.
worlds.source_B_unrelated: New independently sampled essential-three-input truth table and new parent coordinates, rejecting equality with A table or its trivial permutation; source labels remain hidden.
worlds.B_split: Independently shuffle all 32 intervention vectors, first 24 distinct for B fitting, final 8 never shown to B fit/selection, use B held domain different from fit noise. First 16 B training observations select mapping, last 8 B training observations validate mapping-vs-scratch; all 24 used to refit B-only scratch. No B held labels for any decision.
worlds.A_memory: Keep all 96 A action/outcome records unchanged while B learns. Validate pre-B predictions on 32 A actions against packed/restored post-B A predictions and source state bytes. This is synthetic same-process restoration, not native checkpoint custody.

arms.transfer: Fit A's generic 1/2/3-parent causal subset and Laplace table from A96 (Gate17 fit+validation settings). Generate all ordered B action-parent mappings to A's learned k parents (k=1/2/3; up to 60 permutations). Choose best 16-B-event mean negative log loss; use final eight B training examples to decide transfer against scratch. Accept sharing only when mapping validation Brier is at least 0.015 lower than scratch-fit-on-first16 validation Brier; otherwise B-only. For accepted mapping use A96 table with no B-held updates. No true map leaks.
arms.fixed_full: Identical outputs and 388-byte persisted records, but always enumerate all possible B mappings even if A source subset is poor; evaluated separately for unique structural advantage. If implementation naturally identical under k=3, report exact tie.
arms.scratch: No A mechanism. Fit B-only one/two/three-parent conditional lookup with LOO penalization on first16 B and refit selected B route on all24; same B samples and raw persisted memory envelope. Can have weak fitting due limited samples; compare to Bayesian B-only.
arms.bayes_shared: Soft posterior average over B candidate mappings given A's estimated table and 24 B observations. Additionally include B-only generic subset model as an alternative mixture component, with frozen 50:50 prior mass to shared vs independent B. Bayesian evidence and held forecasting use extra temporary memory/computation not equalized.
arms.unrelated_A: Negative training: shuffle A outcome labels deterministically prior to fitting while preserving B evidence. Use identical transfer decision and scratch fallback. Cannot improve over genuine transfer by >0.02 on shared tasks without flagging.
arms.oracle_map: Informationally advantaged diagnostic: true source parent map disclosed to oracle ONLY, with A learned conditional probabilities. Not an eligible control for scientific PASS.
arms.flat_B: Laplace table on full five-bit B action, p=.5 for each eight strictly unseen held action vectors; reference memorization baseline.

persistence.compact_record: All arms can store 2*(96*2+2) = 388 bytes maximum, A's 96 pairs plus B's 24 pairs occupy 240 payload bytes; 148 bytes are zero padding. No precomputed true source/table/map in persisted record. B map, source A candidate and Bayesian probabilities recomputed after restore. This is persisted-evidence parity, not equal process memory or compute.
persistence.restoration: After B learning, encode and restore independently twice; verify byte equality and all B-held forecasts plus 32 A reference forecasts. Native cross-process durability and online B-to-A parameter reuse still untested.
persistence.work: Report number of parent-map candidate likelihood evaluations and B-only mask fit operations. No wall-clock or energy efficiency claim without controlled benchmark.

protocol.paired_per_seed: B held Brier means across 8 action labels per seed, paired normal 95% confidence intervals; compute transfer vs scratch, shuffled-A, and Bayesian. Record transfer acceptance rate on related and unrelated families.
protocol.negative: Unrelated source has no true shared mapping. Report erroneous sharing and Brier degradation; prevent post-result tuning of validation threshold.

falsification: Only score scientific development signal if all substantive transfer/negative/comparator thresholds pass. Structural gain requires outperforming same-memory fixed evaluator and strong Bayesian model; exact tie fails it. If scratch or Bayesian defeats transfer, mark mixed/no-go and retain negatives. No accepted native learning or general intelligence gain on any synthetic outcome.
